caption:
does sunscreen block visible light?

SPF measures protection from UVB. It says nothing about visible light — the light you can actually see.

In deeper skin tones, visible light can cause pigmentation that is darker and lasts longer than the UVA kind (Mahmoud 2010, skin types IV–VI). In fair skin that burns easily, it barely did.

The check: squeeze some sunscreen onto your hand. White or clear means most visible light passes through. Tinted means iron oxide, which blocks more of it. In a melasma trial, a tinted SPF 50 improved skin colour measurements by 28% more than an untinted one, with both groups using the same lightening cream (Castanedo-Cazares 2014). Differences on other scores were smaller.

If dark spots are your concern, tinted is the one to choose.

General education only.
